chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr from Hisham ibn Salim and Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Mukkan, all from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a slave who is shared between partners, and one of them frees his share. He said: "That is a defect for his partners, so they cannot sell him nor rent him out."
He said: "He is appraised at a value, which is placed upon the one who freed him as a penalty; that was made because of what he ruined."
And that which indicates that if he is not causing harm, it is preferred for him to buy what remains when he is able to do so, is what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one partner frees a shared slave?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the fiqh of partial manumission (*kitaabah* context) in shared slaves, ruling that unilateral emancipation creates a defect (*fasad*) in the partnership, thereby restricting the other partners' ability to sell or lease the slave. To rectify this, the emancipator must pay the appraised value as compensation, though it is recommended (*mustahabb*) for him to buy out the remaining shares to fully liberate the slave. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic balance between the spiritual merit of emancipation and the preservation of property rights among co-owners.
